title: Fitbit Edge özellikleri ve tasarım ayrıntıları sızdırıldı
summary: Google'ın 12 Ekim'de tanıtacağı yeni akıllı bilekliği Fitbit Edge modelinin ekran boyutu, tasarımı ve Google uygulamaları desteği ortaya çıktı.
body:
Google'ın 12 Ekim'de resmi olarak tanıtmaya hazırlandığı yeni akıllı bileklik **Fitbit Edge** hakkında yeni tasarım ve donanım ayrıntıları gün yüzüne çıktı. Sızdırılan son bilgilere göre cihaz, ekransız tasarıma sahip Fitbit Air modelinin aksine hem dokunmatik bir ekran hem de bağımsız GPS desteği barındıracak.

## Fitbit Edge neler sunuyor?

Android Headlines ve Forbes kaynaklı sızıntılara göre Fitbit Edge, 1.34 inç büyüklüğünde dokunmatik bir ekranla geliyor. Kasanın sağ tarafında yer alan fiziksel buton ile kontrol kolaylığı sağlayan modelin, çakıl taşını andıran hafif ve kompakt bir gövdeye sahip olduğu görülüyor. Cihazın kordon yapısının Pixel Watch 5 kordonlarına benzer silikon malzemeden üretildiği belirtilirken, farklı renk seçeneklerinin de sunulacağı aktarılıyor.

Akıllı bilekliğin hem Android hem de iOS cihazlarla uyumlu çalışacağı ve telefon bildirimlerini doğrudan gösterebileceği belirtiliyor. Donanım tarafında yerleşik GPS barındıran modelin; Google Haritalar, Google Cüzdan ve Google Müzik gibi temel Google servislerine de destek vermesi bekleniyor.

## Pil ömrü ve çıkış beklentisi

Cihazın tek şarjla yedi güne kadar pil ömrü sunabileceği, yoğun GPS ve sensör kullanımında ise bu sürenin beş güne yaklaşabileceği ifade ediliyor. ABD pazarında 149 ile 199 dolar arasında bir fiyat aralığında satışa çıkması beklenen bilekliğin Türkiye fiyatı ve bulunabilirliği henüz netleşmedi.

**Neden önemli?** Fitbit Charge 6 modelinin yerini alması beklenen Fitbit Edge, bağımsız GPS ve ekran konforunu kompakt bir gövdede birleştirerek spor yaparken telefon taşıma zorunluluğunu ortadan kaldırmayı amaçlıyor.
editor_note: Özelliklerin bir kısmı henüz resmi lansman öncesi sızıntılara ve basın iddialarına dayanıyor.

source_texts.title: Forget the Fitbit Air — 5 things you need to know about the rumored Fitbit Edge
source_texts.summary: The Fitbit Charge 6 may finally get an update. Here are the most important things you need to know about the rumored Fitbit Edge.
source_texts.text:
Despite debuting back in 2023, the Fitbit Charge 6 remains one of my favorite fitness trackers on the market today because of its onboard GPS, reliable tracking performance, small but bright display, comfy design, impressive battery life, and support for several handy Google apps.
While 2026’s Fitbit Air is in some ways the spiritual successor to the Fitbit Charge 6, the lack of a screen, smart features, and onboard GPS means it doesn’t quite fill the same shoes as its older sibling.
So, will Google ever launch a Charge 6 replacement, or is the brand too concerned about sales potentially cannibalizing interest in the Pixel Watch 5? Based on a host of recent rumors and links, the former now seems likely.
That’s right, a true-blue Fitbit Charge 6 replacement could debut as early as this year. Better yet, it may combine all the best bits of the Fitbit Charge 6 in a smaller, more Fitbit Air-like package.
Here are the five biggest things you should know about the rumored Fitbit Edge.
1. Unlike the Fitbit Air, the Edge is rumored to have a screen
Screen-free fitness trackers are clearly in vogue at the moment. 2026 gave us the Fitbit Air, Garmin Cirqa, Luna Band, and more. While I’m a fan of the distraction-free promise of these devices, sometimes it’s nice to interact with your gadget without having to open an app on your phone.
Google seems to agree, because the Fitbit Edge is rumored to incorporate a 1.34-inch display that’s likely touch-sensitive, according to a report by Forbes. Leaked images, shared by Android Headlines, also suggest that the device will have at least one physical button on the side of the case.
Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.
2. Onboard GPS also seems likely
My biggest gripe about the Fitbit Air is that it lacks onboard GPS, which means you need to carry your paired phone with you for outdoor workouts if you want accurate location-based data.
As someone who frequently makes use of the great outdoors for my recreational enjoyment, I much prefer not being forced to bring my bulky iPhone 16 Plus along for the excursion, especially when going for a run or bike ride.
Fortunately, the Fitbit Edge is rumored to include onboard GPS, just like the Fitbit Charge 6. On the flip side, this probably means that battery life won’t be quite as good as the Fitbit Air, which lasts roughly a week per charge. More likely, it will be closer to five days, similar to the Charge 6.
3. The Edge will probably support basic Google apps
Don’t expect the Fitbit Edge to be jam-packed with smart features; that’s what the Pixel Watch line is for, but you can likely expect it to support some basic Google apps, like Google Maps, Google Music, and Google Wallet.
4. Expect a petite, lightweight design
Again, going by leaked images, the Fitbit Edge appears to be slightly smaller than the Fitbit Charge 6, with a more pebble-like case design. The strap shown appears similar in design to the silicone straps that ship with the Pixel Watch 5.
While I don’t have any concrete specs, I suspect the Edge will weigh less than the ~30 g Fitbit Charge 6 but a little more than the ~13 g Fitbit Air.
With only one physical button shown on the right side of the case, it seems likely that the screen on the tracker will be touch-sensitive. Design-wise, I expect Google to launch the Fitbit Edge with a decent selection of eye-catching color combinations to choose from.
5. It will likely cost between $150 and $200
The Fitbit Air is $99, while the Fitbit Charge 6 launched at $159. How much can we expect the Fitbit Edge to go for? Given the rate of inflation over the past three years, it seems likely that the Edge will cost a little bit more than its predecessor, but I highly doubt it will surpass $200.
What are your thoughts on the Fitbit Edge? Does it sound like a proper replacement for the Fitbit Charge 6? Moreover, cost aside, which fitness tracker would you rather own, the screen-free Fitbit Air or a screen- and GPS-equipped Fitbit Edge? Let me know below.

Dan Bracaglia is the Tom’s Guide editorial lead for all things smartwatches, fitness trackers and outdoor gear. With 15 years of experience as a consumer technology journalist testing everything from Oura Rings to instant cameras, Dan is deeply passionate about helping readers save money and make informed purchasing decisions. In the past year alone, Dan has assessed major product releases from the likes of Apple, Garmin, Google, Samsung, Polar and many others.
An avid outdoor adventurer, Dan is based in the U.S. Pacific Northwest where he takes advantage of the beautiful surroundings every chance he gets. A lover of kayaking, hiking, swimming, biking, snowboarding and exploring, he also makes every effort to combine his day job with his passions. When not assessing the sleep tracking and heart rate accuracy of the latest tach gadgets, you can find him photographing Seattle’s vibrant underground music community.
